title: Windows Security Event Log
text:
5.1
DETECTION BY LOG SOURCE
TELEMETRY  /  CONTEXT  /  EVIDENCE
DE
SERIES
WINDOWS SECURITY
EVENT LOG
Event meaning depends on the provider, channel and effective audit policy.
SECURITY-CHANNEL REFERENCE • SELECTED EVENTS
SOURCE GUIDE
EVENT ID
OBSERVATION • SECURITY CHANNEL
4624 / 4625
Successful logon / failed logon
4648
Logon attempt using explicit credentials
4672
Special privileges assigned to a new logon
4688
New process; command-line policy is separate
4662
Directory-service object access; SACL required
4769 / 4776
Service-ticket request / credential validation
4720
A Windows user account was created
4728 / 4732 / 4756
Member added to global / local / universal security group
4697 / 4698
Service installed / scheduled task created
1102
The Security audit log was cleared
Separate source: System 7045 = service installation (Service Control Manager).
COLLECTION CHECK
Check effective audit policy and
forwarding. Event 4688 needs a separate
policy for command-line capture. Event
4662 requires Directory Service Access
auditing and a relevant SACL. [W1, W2]
INTERPRETATION LIMIT
A successful logon, explicit credentials or
special privileges do not prove theft or
exploitation. Keep session, host, actor and
event-version context. Distinguish a
cleared log from failed forwarding.
K E Y  I D E A
Verify the event, the channel and the collection policy.

REFERENCE • NOT A DETECTOR

title: Sysmon
text:
5.2
DETECTION BY LOG SOURCE
TELEMETRY  /  CONTEXT  /  EVIDENCE
DE
SERIES
SYSMON
ENDPOINT EVENT FAMILIES
A configured stream of endpoint observations—not an automatic attack verdict.
TEN EVENT FAMILIES TO VERIFY
SOURCE GUIDE
1
Process creation
ProcessGuid and command line
3
Network connection
Process-linked TCP / UDP
6 / 7
Driver / image load
Availability depends on configuration
8
CreateRemoteThread
Start-module fields can be empty
10
Process access
Access masks and available call trace
11
File creation
File activity and originating process
12–14
Registry activity
Create/delete, value set and rename
17 / 18
Named pipes
Creation and connection
22
DNS query
Process-associated name resolution
25
Process tampering
Supported image-tampering observations
COLLECTION CHECK
Record the installed version and
configuration hash. Test inclusion and
exclusion filters. Network and image-load
visibility must be checked explicitly; do not
infer it from the product name. [S1]
INTERPRETATION LIMIT
Empty start-module fields or an unresolved
call trace do not prove injected code.
Image-load records are not guaranteed
coverage of manual mapping. Correlate
process identity, timing and host role. [A, S1]
K E Y  I D E A
A documented event type is not proof that you collect it.

MICROSOFT TABLE EXAMPLE [E1]
DeviceId + Timestamp
ProcessUniqueId
InitiatingProcessUniqueId
ReportId alone is not a unique record key.
Preserve the documented event key and the original source record.
COLLECTION CHECK
Confirm sensor deployment, health,
retention and actual populated columns.
DeviceProcessEvents is a Microsoft
example, not a universal EDR schema.
Unsupported fields must stay unknown. [E1]
INTERPRETATION LIMIT
Keep vendor detections separate from
your own conclusions. A table name does
not establish collection completeness.
Validate process-lineage joins; a process
ID alone can be reused.

title: Network Detection and Response
text:
5.4
DETECTION BY LOG SOURCE
TELEMETRY  /  CONTEXT  /  EVIDENCE
DE
SERIES
NETWORK DETECTION
AND RESPONSE
Network metadata describes traffic visible at a specific sensor location.
SENSOR PLACEMENT SETS THE VISIBILITY BOUNDARY
SOURCE GUIDE
Client / service
Traffic to observe
Network path
Monitored link / switch
Destination
Traffic destination
TAP / SPAN copy → Zeek sensor
conn.log
Directional connection metadata
dns.log
Queries, answers and TTLs
ssl.log
Observable TLS metadata
Schema detail: dns.log uses TTLs, not TTL. [N1]
COLLECTION CHECK
Record placement, packet loss, Zeek version
and enabled scripts. Inspect real records for
required fields. Certificate details, hashes
and fingerprints depend on analyzers,
protocol and configuration. [N1, N2]
INTERPRETATION LIMIT
JA3/JA4 fingerprints are not actor
identities. Shared libraries and changing
clients affect comparisons. Encrypted
payload content cannot be inferred from
connection metadata alone. [N2, N3]
K E Y  I D E A
A sensor sees its observation point—not the entire estate.

title: Identity and Access Management Platforms
text:
5.5
DETECTION BY LOG SOURCE
TELEMETRY  /  CONTEXT  /  EVIDENCE
DE
SERIES
IDENTITY & ACCESS
MANAGEMENT PLATFORMS
Interpret identity actions through actor, target, outcome and session context.
CATALOG EVENTS ARE OBSERVATIONS, NOT VERDICTS
SOURCE GUIDE
Actor
Who performed it?
Action + result
What actually succeeded?
Target
What changed for whom?
OKTA CATALOG EXAMPLES [I2]
user.mfa.factor.update
Factor update
user.session.impersonation.initiate
Impersonation session start
user.account.privilege.grant
Admin privileges changed
Correlate within the correct tenant, identity and time bounds.
COLLECTION CHECK
Retain the precise event type, outcome,
reason, actor, target and available session
keys. Verify licensing, configuration and
retention. Support activity and approved
role changes can be legitimate. [I1, I2]
INTERPRETATION LIMIT
Entra risk detections use multiple signal
types—not only anomaly models. A denied
MFA challenge is not automatically a fraud
report; a generic failure does not
demonstrate MFA fatigue. [I1, I2]
K E Y  I D E A
Read the outcome and the actors—not just the event name.

Accounts

Provider-only context may be absent from your exported logs.
COLLECTION CHECK
Scope accounts, regions, resources and
event categories. CloudTrail data events
need explicit collection choices. Verify a
representative raw record before relying
on an exported field. [C1]

GuardDuty names GenerateDbAuthToken

does not track token generation. Preserve
this discrepancy; do not assume an
exported event exists. [C2, C3]

title: DNS Security
text:
5.7
DETECTION BY LOG SOURCE
TELEMETRY  /  CONTEXT  /  EVIDENCE
DE
SERIES
DNS SECURITY
ENTROPY IS A FEATURE
Character-frequency entropy measures symbol distribution—not attacker intent.
EXACT MATH • SYNTHETIC FOUR-CHARACTER LABELS
NOT INCIDENT DATA
H = −Σ p(c) log₂ p(c)
H ≤ log₂(min(n, |A|))    •    n = label length; A = alphabet
Bits per character
0
0.5
1
1.5
2
0.00
aaaa
1.00
abab
2.00
abcd
abcd is structured, yet has 2.00 bits per character.
MEASUREMENT CONTRACT
Choose the label before scoring. Normalize
case and handle internationalized names
explicitly. Use a public-suffix-aware parser
for registrable-domain grouping. Keep label
length alongside entropy.
INTERPRETATION LIMIT
Structured text can have high entropy.
Legitimate encoded labels are important
controls. Resolver, endpoint and network
logs see different paths; caching and
encrypted DNS can limit visibility. [A, N1]
K E Y  I D E A
High entropy describes symbols—not malicious intent.
1200km.com  |  Section 5.7
EXACT ARITHMETIC • NO ALERT THRESHOLD

Other workload operations to verify [O1]:
MailItemsAccessed  •  FileDownloaded  •  FileSyncDownloadedFull
COLLECTION CHECK
Verify workload auditing and retention.
Microsoft 365 operations differ by workload.
App consent and service-principal changes
may require Entra audit records in addition to

INTERPRETATION LIMIT
OfficeObjectId identifies an object; it is not
its size. Count distinct evidence IDs
separately from distinct objects. Report
bytes only from validated transfer counters
or documented size enrichment. [O1]

title: Detection Source Prioritization Matrix
text:
5.9
DETECTION BY LOG SOURCE
TELEMETRY  /  CONTEXT  /  EVIDENCE
DE
SERIES
DETECTION SOURCES
PRIORITIZATION MATRIX
Select evidence for a local visibility gap—not for an unsupported fidelity score.
PLANNING MATRIX • NO UNIVERSAL DEPLOYMENT ORDER
SOURCE GUIDE
LOCAL DECISION
EVIDENCE TO REQUIRE
01
Visibility gap
Threat model, important assets and
currently unobserved behaviors
02
Collectability
Raw examples, policy, schema, sensor
health and required entitlements
03
Operational fit
Measured volume, retention, privacy
requirements and a named owner
04
Analytic value
Held-out candidates, benign controls,
missed cases and analyst workload
05
Priority justification
Documented local benefit and cost;
no unsupported source-fidelity score
These are planning questions—not measured product rankings.
PILOT BEFORE SCALING
Test one defined use case on important
assets. Include ordinary workload changes
and known missed cases. Measure retained
evidence, alert usefulness and the work
required to review each candidate.
OWNERSHIP & COST
Assign a collection owner, a retention
decision and a recurring health check.
Compare local value with volume, privacy
and operating cost. Record remaining blind
spots rather than hiding them.
K E Y  I D E A
Prioritize demonstrated local value—not a vendor label.
1200km.com  |  Section 5.9
PLANNING FRAMEWORK • NOT MEASURED RANKINGS
